Contract No. 2026/164
 
VP523400

The City of Boroondara is seeking a suitably experienced provider to work with Council to develop a Service Review Framework (Part 1), with the option to subsequently extend the Framework to incorporate a Service Planning Approach (Part 2).

Part 1 – Service Review Framework

1. Part 1.A – Development of the Framework

The provider will develop a practical, fit-for-purpose Service Review Framework that establishes a consistent approach to planning and undertaking service reviews across Council, including the methodology, tools and supporting resources required to undertake future service reviews.

The Framework should complement Council’s Benefits Framework by supporting the identification, assessment and tracking of benefits from review recommendations, and enable insights and opportunities identified through reviews to inform ongoing service improvement.

The Framework, associated resources and intellectual property will be owned by Council and will provide the basis for establishing a panel of suitably qualified providers to undertake future service reviews on Council’s behalf.

2. Part 1.B – Pilot of the Framework

As part of Part 1, the successful provider will be required to pilot the Service Review Framework with one small Council service. The pilot will provide an opportunity to test the Framework, methodology and tools in practice and refine them based on the experience of undertaking a review.

The pilot should demonstrate how the Framework can be practically applied and help ensure the final Framework is fit-for-purpose, scalable and capable of being applied consistently across Council.

Part 2 – Service Planning Approach

As an optional next phase, Council may choose to engage the successful provider to extend the Service Review Framework to incorporate a Service Planning Approach.

Part 2 is not guaranteed and would only proceed at Council’s discretion. It is dependent on the development of Council’s Service Catalogue, which is currently underway, and would therefore be undertaken after Part 1 has been completed.

Reverse Brief

Council is seeking a reverse brief from respondents that demonstrates their understanding of the opportunity across both Part 1 and the potential Part 2, recommends an appropriate approach and sequencing, and identifies any refinements, considerations or dependencies that Council should take into account. This should include how the proposed Framework would complement Council’s Benefits Framework and support ongoing service improvement.

Respondents should outline their proposed approach to developing and piloting the Service Review Framework and, where relevant, their proposed approach to subsequently incorporating Service Planning. Respondents are encouraged to draw on their experience in service review and service planning to propose an approach that will deliver a practical, scalable and sustainable Framework for use across Council.

Work Package:

Miscellaneous
Specialist Tunnel Surveying Services;

Overview
Future Generation is a joint venture created specifically to build Snowy 2.0 on behalf of Snowy Hydro Limited. We bring the combined engineering expertise of three companies – Italy’s Salini Impregilo, Australian-based Clough and US-based Lane Construction. Our team’s pair local expertise with global experience.



Snowy 2.0 will supercharge the Snowy Scheme’s existing hydro-electric generation and large-scale storage capabilities. The fast-start, on-demand generation of pumped-hydro and Snowy 2.0’s massive storage capacity will be vital as more intermittent, renewable energy sources such as wind and solar come online and coal-fired power stations retire.



Snowy 2.0 will add 2,000 megawatts of energy generation and provide 175 hours of storage for the National Electricity Market (NEM), enough to ensure the stability and reliability of the system during prolonged weather events, such as wind or solar ‘droughts’.

Snowy Hydro already plays a critical role in ensuring system stability and at times of peak demand, we keep the lights on. Snowy 2.0 will enhance our existing capability and ensure that we can continue to provide increased stability and security to the energy market well into the future.



The project links two existing Scheme dams, Tantangara and Talbingo, through tunnels and an underground power station with pumping capabilities. Hydro-power will be generated by falling water spinning Snowy 2.0’s giant reversible turbines, which can also pump water in the opposite direction.

Snowy 2.0’s pumping capabilities work in a ‘closed’ system – water is recycled between the upper dam (Tantangara) and lower dam (Talbingo) so the same water can be used to generate power more than once, making the most of available water. Snowy Hydro already has pumped-hydro capabilities at the Tumut 3 Power Station - it is proven technology used across the world



The ability to store water and generate power on-demand means Snowy 2.0 can be ‘switched on’ very quickly. Snowy 2.0 will pump water using the excess electricity in the system at times of low demand. Then, when energy is needed most, the stored water will be used to generate electricity within minutes.

For example, if the wind is blowing in the middle of the night when consumers are asleep, Snowy 2.0 can use the wind energy to pump and then store the water in the upper dam. When households wake up and the demand for energy soars, Snowy 2.0 can quickly generate energy for the grid.

The first power produced from Snowy 2.0 is expected in late 2024-25, with progressive commissioning on the six units. Snowy 2.0’s operating life is expected to be consistent with the Snowy Scheme’s existing assets, which continue to operate reliably many decades after installation.

Building Snowy 2.0

The project will involve underground excavation and tunneling works between Tantangara and Talbingo dams to depths of up to one kilometre. This RFI process will enable Transport to refine the PSCP procurement and delivery strategy to create a sustainable contracting regime that delivers improved outcomes for the people of NSW.

Project goals
Transport for NSW (Transport) is progressing the next phase of bus service contracting reform across its operating regions. Transport is currently developing the next generation of contracts for bus, light rail and ferry services as existing agreements progressively expire from June 2028.

Transport is seeking feedback from industry on the development of these contracts, including opportunities to improve service delivery, contract management, asset maintenance and commercial arrangements. Industry feedback will be important in ensuring that future contracts respond to the Bus Industry Taskforce recommendations and Audit Office Report recommendations, while also aligning with the broader Transport and NSW government outcomes such as Net Zero Plan and Connecting NSW Strategy and create a sustainable contracting regime which delivers improved outcomes for the people of NSW.

As part of the development process, Transport is undertaking industry consultation exercise to gather feedback from industry. This engagement will assist Transport understanding industry perspectives on key operational, commercial and delivery considerations associated with the future contracting framework.

Scope
Transport is seeking feedback in relation to:

i. Packaging;

ii. Service design and scheduling;

iii. Safety and accreditations:

iv. Contract Duration:

v. Contract Performance Management Framework;

vi. Better Buses/ Innovation and sustainability;

vii. Commercial Risk Allocation;

viii. Payment Structures:

Homes Victoria (Organisation) is intending to release a Request for Tender in September 2026 for Residential Tenancies Act (RTA) Safety Checks. Homes Victoria is responsible for the maintenance of social housing, which includes public and community housing properties across the state of Victoria. There are currently 4 geographical divisions which includes ~71,000 properties, across the state of Victoria in which maintenance services are provided.

As such Homes Victoria will be seeking to appoint multiple head contractors to provide RTA Safety Check services for the ~71,000 properties across the state of Victoria.

Scope of services will include but not limited to:

Performance of RTA safety check inspections to comply with safety and legislative requirements on the department’s properties.
Conducting annual property condition inspections, specifically reporting on:
a. Immediate safety and essential services concerns, with immediate corrective actions.

b. Property and tenant conditions considering minimum rental standards and environmental indicators such as but not limited to; hoarding, significant property damage, and living conditions detrimental to the health and safety of the renter or that contribute to the premature ageing of the property.

This Request for Tender will be released via an open tender process.

Homes Victoria also wishes to advise all prospective suppliers that an Application Programming Interface (API) will need to be established to ensure seamless data connection with Homes Victoria and suppliers’ works management systems.

The Victorian Government’s Social Procurement Framework apply to this procurement. The Government’s Fair Jobs Code Plan applies to this procurement, and tender participants will need to hold a Pre-Assessment Certificate at the time of Tender submission.

Homes Victoria reserves its rights to amend its approach, timing and requirements in respect to the contractor procurement process.

The AgriFutures Research, Development and Extension (RD&E) Plans provide the strategic direction for investment across AgriFutures Australia’s industries. They guide researchers and delivery partners in developing project proposals and support AgriFutures Australia to invest in activities that address industry priorities and emerging opportunities.

The AgriFutures Goat Fibre Program supports Australia’s goat fibre industry through targeted research, development and extension activities that strengthen industry capability, productivity, profitability and long-term sustainability. The current AgriFutures Goat Fibre RD&E Plan (2021-2026) was developed in consultation with industry stakeholders and outlines the Program’s strategic objectives and investment priorities.

As the current plan approaches completion, AgriFutures Australia is commencing development of a new Goat Fibre RD&E Plan (2027-2032). The new plan will be informed by broad industry consultation and will identify the research, development and extension priorities needed to support the future growth, resilience and sustainability of the Australian goat fibre industry.

Service requirements
AgriFutures Australia is seeking a suitably qualified individual or organisation to undertake industry consultation and develop the AgriFutures Goat Fibre RD&E Plan 2027-2032.
The successful respondent will be responsible for designing and delivering an industry consultation process that captures the priorities, challenges and opportunities facing the Australian goat fibre industry and translating these findings into a new RD&E Plan.

Consultation activities may include a combination of:

Industry workshops
One-on-one stakeholder interviews
Surveys and other engagement mechanisms
Consultation with the Goat Fibre Advisory Panel and AgriFutures staff
Applicants should demonstrate an understanding of the Australian goat fibre industry and its RD&E needs, including the production of mohair and cashmere, together with proven experience engaging and communicating with growers and other primary producers. The successful respondent will also be expected to understand the role of AgriFutures Australia and the purpose of industry RD&E Plans in guiding investment decisions.

Project deliverables

Consultation plan and stakeholder engagement approach
Stakeholder consultation activities (workshops, interviews, surveys etc.)
Consultation summary report outlining key themes, priorities and findings
Draft Goat Fibre RD&E Plan 2027-2032
Revised/final Goat Fibre RD&E Plan 2027-2032 incorporating AgriFutures and Industry feedback
Presentation of findings to the Goat Fibre Industry
This Request for Quote closes on Friday, 25 September 2026 at 12 pm AEST.
